statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = (sum_{i=0}^{len(s)-1} F(s[i] - 97, t)) mod (10^9 + 7), where for any integer c with 0 <= c < 26 and integer k >= 0, F(c, k) is defined recursively by F(c, 0) = 1 and F(c, k+1) = sum_{j=1}^{nums[c]} F((c + j) mod 26, k). Here (c + j) mod 26 denotes the remainder of c + j divided by 26, which lies in 0..25.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= 10^9 + 6.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25.

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = (sum_{i=0}^{len(s)-1} nums[s[i] - 97]) mod (10^9 + 7).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; t = 1; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = len(s) mod (10^9 + 7).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, nums[j] = 1 (which implies 1 <= nums[j] <= 25).

statement: Let r be the result of the function on s1 ++ s2, let r1 be the result on s1, and let r2 be the result on s2 (all with the same t and nums). Then the function returns r, r1, r2 and r = (r1 + r2) mod (10^9 + 7).
preconditions: For every t and nums satisfying 1 <= t <= 10^9, len(nums) == 26, and for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25, and for every two non-empty strings s1 and s2 with len(s1) + len(s2) <= 10^5, for every i with 0 <= i < len(s1), 97 <= s1[i] <= 122, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s2), 97 <= s2[i] <= 122:

statement: Let r1 be the result of the function on s1 and r2 be the result on s2, both with the same t and nums. If for every c in 0..25 the number of occurrences of the byte 97+c in s1 equals the number of occurrences of 97+c in s2, then the function returns r1 and r2 and r1 = r2.
preconditions: For every t and nums satisfying 1 <= t <= 10^9, len(nums) == 26, and for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25, and for every two strings s1 and s2 with 1 <= len(s1) <= 10^5, 1 <= len(s2) <= 10^5, for every i with 0 <= i < len(s1), 97 <= s1[i] <= 122, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s2), 97 <= s2[i] <= 122:

statement: Let r1 be the result of the function on the string consisting of a single copy of c (with the same t and nums). Then the function returns a result r on s and r = (n * r1) mod (10^9 + 7).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25; there exists a character c with 97 <= c <= 122 and an integer n >= 1 such that s is the list of length n where every element equals c.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = (sum_{j=1}^{nums[s[0] - 97]} nums[(s[0] - 97 + j) mod 26]) mod (10^9 + 7).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25; t = 2; len(s) = 1.

statement: Let count_s(c) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(s) such that s[i] = 97 + c. The function returns a result r and r = (sum_{c=0}^{25} count_s(c) * F(c, t)) mod (10^9 + 7), where F is defined as in spec_1: F(c, 0) = 1 and F(c, k+1) = sum_{j=1}^{nums[c]} F((c + j) mod 26, k).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), 97 <= s[i] <= 122 (s[i] is the ASCII code of a lowercase English letter); 1 <= t <= 10^9; len(nums) == 26; for every j with 0 <= j < 26, 1 <= nums[j] <= 25.
